lead: The four options are one word root in different forms: noun, adjective, adverb, verb. The words around the blank decide which form fits.
四個選項是同一個字根的不同詞性（名詞、形容詞、副詞、動詞），空格前後的字決定該用哪一種。
steps: Read only the two words before and the two words after the blank.
只看空格前後各兩個字。
Decide what the blank needs: a noun, an adjective, an adverb or a verb.
判斷這個位置需要名詞、形容詞、副詞還是動詞。
If two options have that part of speech, choose by meaning: a person or a thing, singular or plural.
如果有兩個選項詞性相同，再用意思選：是人還是事、單數還是複數。

head: A noun goes here
名詞的位置
body: After a, the, your, our, an adjective or a preposition. A noun also works as the subject, or as the object of a verb.
冠詞、所有格、形容詞、介系詞的後面，以及當主詞或動詞的受詞。
ex: The implementation of the new policy begins next month.
新政策將從下個月開始實施。
Please send your application by Friday.
請在星期五前寄出你的申請。

head: An adjective goes here
形容詞的位置
body: Before a noun, after be, remain, seem, become and stay, and after make, keep or find plus an object that it describes.
名詞前面；be、remain、seem、become、stay 之後；以及 make、keep、find 加受詞後描述受詞。
ex: Our prices remain competitive this season.
本季我們的價格依然具有競爭力。
The new system makes the approval process more efficient.
新系統讓審核流程更有效率。

head: An adverb goes here
副詞的位置
body: An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective or a whole sentence. Typical spots: between has and a participle, between be and a participle, before an adjective, and as the first word before a comma.
副詞修飾動詞、形容詞或整個句子。常見位置：has 和分詞之間、be 和分詞之間、形容詞前面、句首逗號前。
ex: The shipment has finally arrived at the warehouse.
貨物終於送到倉庫了。
The contract was carefully reviewed by the legal team.
合約經過法務團隊仔細審閱。
Unfortunately, the flight has been canceled.
很遺憾，航班已經取消了。

head: A noun before a noun
名詞放在名詞前面
body: A word before a noun is not always an adjective. In compound nouns the first word is itself a noun. Check that the word after the blank is really the head noun.
名詞前面的字不一定是形容詞。複合名詞的第一個字本身就是名詞，要先確認後面那個字是不是中心名詞。
ex: The company wants to improve customer satisfaction.
公司想提高顧客滿意度。
Staff must complete the safety training.
員工必須完成安全訓練。

head: Noun for a person or for a thing
指人的名詞和指事的名詞
body: One root often gives two nouns. The person: applicant, attendee, supervisor, inspector. The thing: application, attendance, supervision, inspection. Choose by meaning and by singular or plural.
同一個字根常有兩種名詞：人（applicant、attendee）和事（application、attendance）。看句意和單複數來選。
ex: All applicants must bring a photo ID to the interview.
所有應徵者面試時都必須帶附照片的證件。
Attendance at the seminar was higher than expected.
研討會的出席人數比預期的高。

head: Check whether a main verb is missing
先檢查有沒有主要動詞
body: If the sentence has no main verb yet, the blank is the verb. If a main verb is already there, the blank is a noun, adjective or adverb.
句子還沒有主要動詞，空格就要填動詞；已經有了，空格就是名詞、形容詞或副詞。
ex: Ms. Ito approves all travel requests.
伊藤女士核准所有的出差申請。
The approval of travel requests takes two days.
出差申請的核准需要兩天。

why: Remain links the subject to a description, so it takes an adjective.
remain 是連綴動詞，後面描述主詞的狀態，要用形容詞。

pairs.right: Attendance at the seminar was higher than expected.
pairs.wrong: Attendees at the seminar was higher than expected.
why: The sentence measures how many came, so the noun is attendance. Attendees names people and needs a plural verb.
這句在講出席人數，要用 attendance。attendees 指人，而且是複數，動詞也對不上。

pairs.right: All employees must follow the safety regulations.
pairs.wrong: All employees must follow the safe regulations.
why: Safety regulations are rules about safety. Safe regulations would mean rules that are not dangerous.
safety regulations 是安全規範；safe regulations 會變成「不危險的規範」，意思不通。

head: One root, several forms
同字根的不同詞性
items: 成功（動詞）、成功、成功的、成功地

traps: Some adjectives end in -ly: friendly, timely, costly, likely, lively. Do not pick an adverb just because of the ending.
有些形容詞以 -ly 結尾：friendly、timely、costly、likely、lively。不要只看字尾就選副詞。
Some words are both adjective and adverb: hard, late, fast, early, and also weekly, monthly, daily. Hardly (almost not) and lately (recently) are different words.
有些字同時是形容詞和副詞：hard、late、fast、early，還有 weekly、monthly、daily。hardly（幾乎不）和 lately（最近）則是意思不同的另一個字。
A blank before a noun is not always an adjective. Look at the word after it: it may be the first half of a compound noun.
名詞前的空格不一定是形容詞。看後面那個字，它可能是複合名詞的前半。
